title: Old Termites Grow Blue Backpacks. In a Fight, They Explode

scenes.text: When these termites get old, they grow explosive backpacks.
In the rainforest of French Guiana, some worker termites carry two blue spots on their backs. They're pouches of copper-rich crystals.
The crystals build up with age. Meanwhile the worker's jaws wear blunt, and a termite can't sharpen them.
So when the nest is attacked, the oldest workers have one job left.
Grabbed by an enemy, a worker bursts its own body. The crystals mix with fluid from its salivary glands into a sticky liquid that paralyses or kills.
The older the termite, the more toxic the blast. Scientists described it in 2012, and only worked out the chemistry in 2024.

description:
Workers of the termite Neocapritermes taracua, from French Guiana, carry blue copper-containing crystals in pouches on their backs. The crystals grow as the worker ages and its mandibles wear down.
When attacked, the worker ruptures its body: the crystals react with secretions from the salivary glands to make a sticky toxic liquid that immobilises or kills rival termites. Older workers carry the largest and most toxic loads. The behaviour was reported in Science in 2012, and the structure of the blue enzyme behind it was solved in 2024.
Which insect has the wildest defence?
subject: termite blue spots
first_comment: The blue enzyme stays stable on the termite's back for its whole life, ready to react in an instant. Which insect defence should we cover next?
